 Football
 Soccer-Williams-Barnett echoes Bale exploits with first Tottenham goal
 By Martyn Herman 
 Sunday, 22 Nov 2026
 | 2:34 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Soccer Football - Premier League - Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town - Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, Britain - November 21, 2026 Tottenham Hotspur's Luca Williams-Barnett celebrates scoring their first goal REUTERS/Tony O Brien 
 LONDON, Nov 21 (Reuters) - ⁠Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett became the club's youngest Premier League scorer ⁠since Gareth Bale as he marked his first top-flight start with ‌the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.
 Williams-Barnett, who turned 18 last month, stabbed home Pedro Porro's cross in the 15th minute and helped set up his side's second for ​Dominic Solanke with a jinking run.
 It was only ⁠a fifth Tottenham appearance for the ⁠England junior international but the winger rewarded manager Roberto de Zerbi's faith.
 "Luca was ⁠magnificent ‌today. We see him in training every day, we know what a player he is. He's such a talent, honestly," Solanke said.
 "To see him ⁠come in and do that on his first Premier League ​start is crazy. We'll ‌be celebrating with him today. He can bring so much for us.
 "He's ⁠very dedicated and ​so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that. We can see so much in him. It's exciting times for all of ⁠us, especially him."
 Bale was also 18 when he scored ​his first league goal for Tottenham in 2007. The club's youngest Premier League scorer was Andy Turner aged 17 in 1992.
 Welsh winger Bale went on to become a ⁠Tottenham great and a five-times Champions League winner with Real Madrid.
 Tottenham's fans are clearly excited to see a young talent shining so bright and they gave Williams-Barnett a standing ovation when he was substituted after 64 minutes.
 "Honestly, he's just an incredible ​football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's ⁠doing," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie said. "Doing what he is doing in training and in ​the game is just unbelievable."
 Tottenham's victory, their fourth in ‌the last five league games after failing ​to win any of the opening five, moved De Zerbi's side into ninth spot in the table.
 (Reporting by Martyn Herman, editing by Ed Osmond)
